report.answer_text:
I'm assuming you mean India's Supreme Court. Several of its judges have served on the International Court of Justice (ICJ):
Dalveer Bhandari is the best-known example. He was a senior judge of the Supreme Court of India for about seven years. He resigned in 2012 and was then appointed to the ICJ.[1] In 2017 he was re-elected for a nine-year term beginning on 6 February 2018.[2] That term runs until early 2027.
Raghunandan Swarup Pathak was a Supreme Court judge and later the 18th Chief Justice of India. He was elected to the ICJ and served there from 1989 to 1991.[3]
Nagendra Singh served as ICJ President from 1985 to 1988.[3] He is not listed as a Supreme Court judge in these results.
Benegal Narsing Rau served at the ICJ in 1952–1953.[3] He is also not listed as a Supreme Court judge in these results.
If you meant another country's Supreme Court, such as the US, tell me which one and I'll look into it.
